rows.question: Can I resit an exam I already passed to get a higher grade?
rows.answer: No, you cannot resit an exam you have already passed to get a higher grade. According to the general programme rules [2], the most recent mark will apply, and a resit is only allowed if you have failed the examination during all previously offered attempts. Since you have already passed the exam, there is no provision for resitting it to improve your grade. [2]

rows.question: Is a final mark of 5.45 a pass?
rows.answer: No, a final mark of 5.45 would not be considered a pass. According to the general programme rules [1], a final mark between 5 and 6 will be rounded to the nearest whole number, and final marks below 5.50 are rounded down. Therefore, 5.45 would be rounded down to 5, which is below the required passing mark of 6.00.

rows.question: When am I allowed to start my Master Project AI?
rows.answer: You are allowed to start your Master Project AI after completing 60 ECTS of the MSc Artificial Intelligence program [3]. The Master’s programme starts on 1 September, but this is the intake date, not the start date for the Master Project AI [2][4]. For more details and specific rules regarding the Master Project AI, you should refer to the Master project page on Canvas [5].

rows.question: How many EC is the Master Project AI?
rows.answer: The Master Project AI is not assigned a specific number of ECTS, but it is mentioned that it lasts between 5 and 6 months and marks the end of the Master programme in Artificial Intelligence [2][3]. The total programme has a workload of 120 ECTS [5], and you need to have completed 60 ECTS before starting the Master Project AI [1][3].

rows.question: Can I redo the Evolutionary Computing programming assignment if I fail it?
rows.answer: No, you cannot redo the programming assignment if you fail it. According to the course rules, there is no resit option for the programming assignment [1].

rows.question: If I pass the Evolutionary Computing exam but fail the assignment, do I lose my exam grade?
rows.answer: No, if you pass the Evolutionary Computing exam but fail the programming assignment, you can keep the grade of the passed exam for next year or later. Then, you can pass the course by getting a good grade (> 5.5) for the missing assignment and using the old exam grade in the averaging formula [1].

rows.question: How is Deep Learning graded?
rows.answer: Deep Learning (XM_0083) is graded based on a final exam (50%) and practical assignments (50%). The final exam must be passed with a sufficient grade (equivalent to a grade of 5.5 or higher). Practical assignments cannot be redone, and there is a resit available for the exam. [1]

rows.question: Who coordinates the Evolutionary Computing course?
rows.answer: The course coordinator for Evolutionary Computing (X_400111) is prof. dr. A.E. Eiben [5].

rows.question: I already completed Advanced Machine Learning. Can I take Mathematical Foundations of Machine Learning?
rows.answer: You do not need to have completed Advanced Machine Learning to take Mathematical Foundations of Machine Learning [1][5]. The course assumes intermediate skills with at least one learning/optimization algorithm, which you should have from your previous studies [5].

rows.question: What is the deadline to request an extra exam opportunity, and who qualifies?
rows.answer: The deadline to request an extra exam opportunity is 15 July [1]. This provision applies to students who have completed all but one unit of education to meet the requirements of the degree and have failed the examination during all previously offered attempts, unless participation in an examination was not possible for compelling reasons [1].

rows.question: How long after an exam can I inspect my graded work?
rows.answer: You have the right to inspect your graded examination within twenty working days after the results are announced, but no later than ten working days before the resit opportunity for that examination [1]. During this period, you can also view the questions and assignments set in the exam, as well as the standards applied when assessing it [1].

rows.question: How long does an examiner have to grade a written exam?
rows.answer: An examiner has up to fifteen working days to determine the result of a written examination [1].

rows.question: I have a CS bachelor. Should I take Cognitive Psychology and its Applications or Skills for AI?
rows.answer: Based on the programme overview [4], students with an Artificial Intelligence/Computer Science bachelor degree should choose the course Cognitive Psychology and its Applications. Therefore, you should take Cognitive Psychology and Its Applications. [4]
